restatement: Core must expose one structured render contract that the API, CLI and n8n node all consume. render returns {ok, output, messages, stats{chars, estTokens, sectionsOmitted, iterations}, diagnostics} and never throws for template or data problems: a failure gives ok false, empty output and the located error first. validate checks a template without data. analyze adds required and per-kind block counts. spec describes the language and lists every engine filter. A chars/4 estimator can be replaced by an option. resolveTemplate keeps its throwing string behavior. The node renders through the result, keeps writing to its configured field, and turns failures into located NodeOperationErrors. All of this ships with no runtime dependency and no n8n import or I/O in core. The revision adds rr-robust: render and validate never throw for non-object data or cyclic values, and each such case returns ok false with a diagnostic.
verification_plan: Run the frozen gate tests (render, spec, node, nodeps) plus the full suite, and confirm they pass with no frozen test edited.

rr-result: check that every failure path inside render, including parse, interpret and limit failures, returns ok false, an empty output and the located error first, and that nothing outside the try can throw.

Probe render with hostile inputs: null, array, string or number data; cyclic values used as an output variable, a FOR target, in comparisons, math, filters and CASE; BigInt; throwing getters; a non-string template. Record which inputs throw and which return ok true silently.
rr-robust: confirm that each named input (non-object data, a cyclic data value, a cyclic value looped over in strict mode) returns ok false with a diagnostic, and that the new test asserts it.
rr-validate: confirm syntax errors and unknown filters give ok false with located errors, and a missing variable gives ok true.
rr-analyze: confirm required equals !optional and blocks counts each kind.
rr-spec: confirm spec's filter list comes from the same source the engine uses, so the two cannot drift, and that limits equal DEFAULT_LIMITS.
rr-estimator: confirm the default is ceil(chars/4) and that tokenEstimator replaces it and receives the output.
m1: diff the interpreter changes and confirm no resolveTemplate output changes for a passing template.
m2 and m3: confirm package.json adds no dependencies and core imports neither n8n nor fs, http or other I/O.
Node: confirm it keeps the outputField default resolved_prompt, its old tests still pass, and failures carry the line and column.

findings.title: A cyclic data value used as output renders ok true with empty text instead of ok false with a diagnostic, and the rr-robust test accepts it

serves.scenario: c9 requires that render returns ok false with a diagnostic for cyclic data values. For render('${{a}}', {a: cyclic}, {strictMode: true}), render instead returns ok true, output '' and no diagnostics: a data problem passes silently as an empty substitution. The new rr-robust test only asserts typeof r.ok === 'boolean' and checks diagnostics only when ok is false, so it passes either way and does not verify the criterion.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c9 rr-robust)
findings.reproduction: Compile core/src with tsc and run: const a={x:'v'}; a.self=a; render('a\n${{a}}', {a}, {strictMode:true}). The result is {ok:true, output:'a\n', diagnostics:[]}. render('${{a.self.self.x}}', {a}) behaves the same way. The cause is Interpreter.valueToString (core/src/interpreter.ts ~608): it calls tryCoerceToString, which swallows the JSON.stringify failure and returns null, and valueToString then turns null into ''. Smallest fix: make render report this case. One way is an interpreter option set only by render that throws a located type-error when an object value cannot be stringified. Then tighten the rr-robust cases to expect ok false. Keeping the change behind a render-only option leaves resolveTemplate's output unchanged (m1).
evidence: test:rr-robust: strict the cyclic value itself does not throw

findings.title: render and validate still throw for a non-string template such as null

serves.scenario: Goal-critical question: can render throw for any template or data input? Yes. render(null, {}) and validate(null) throw a native TypeError ('Cannot read properties of null (reading length')') from the lexer, which sits outside any guard. The revision added a runtime guard for non-object data, but nothing guards the template. A JS library caller, or any consumer that does not pre-validate, gets an exception instead of the shared ok false or invalid-input result.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (rr-result: never throws for template or data problems)
findings.reproduction: Compile core/src with tsc and call render(null, {}). It throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length'). validate(null) throws the same error. render(42, {}) returns ok true with output ''. Smallest fix: at the top of render and validate, return an invalid-input diagnostic at 1:1 when typeof template !== 'string', mirroring the existing data guard.

evidence: test:rr-robust: a strict FOR over a cyclic non-array value does not throw and is located
test:rr-robust: data that is null gives ok false with invalid-input at 1:1
